newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P downgrades ratings for Electricity Corp of NZ.
newsitem.headline: S&P downgrades ratings for Electricity Corp of NZ.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Monday it had lowered its long-term rating of Electricity Corporation of New Zealand Ltd to A+ from AA- and its short-term rating to A-1 from A-1+.
Both ratings for the state-owned electricity generator were removed from creditwatch negative, where they were placed on June 9.
The downgrade reflected the split of ECNZ into two competing state-owned enterprises as part of the development of a competitive wholesale electricity market.
ECNZ will remain the dominant generator and its low-cost profile places it in a good competitive position with a strong financial structure, S&P said.
"However, some uncertainty about how the wholesale energy market will develop over the long term has result in an increased risk profile for the generator," it added.
The competitive wholesale market is due to start trading on October 1.
About 30 percent of ECNZ's generating assets have been transferred to newly-created rival Contact Energy.

S&P said net interest cover for ECNZ was likely to remain about 3.5 to four times and the net debt payback period would stay below five years. Capital expenditure would remain low and gearing ratios of total debt to total capital would be
maintained at 35 to 40 percent through the government's dividend policy as shareholder.
S&P said ECNZ was well-positioned financially and operationally, and the government's commitment not to privatise it further added to credit stability.
